excerpt: Dimidjian and Segal estimate, using the NIH stage model, that only 30% of research using mindfulness-based interventions has moved beyond Stage 1; the majority beyond Stage 1 has been conducted at Stage 2a, only 9% of the total at Stage 2b with active controls, and only 1% outside research contexts.
overview: These percentages anchor the article's clinical caution. They show that much MBI research remains early-stage or weakly controlled, with very little evidence from ordinary clinical settings, making broad implementation claims premature even where some efficacy signals exist.
title: Clinical Stage Distribution
